full_judgment:
These 2 Rules arise out of the judgment of revarsal in pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The Trial Court allowed the pre-emption and the lower appellate court disallowed it against which the pre-emptor has obtained this Rule. 

 2. The only ground upon which the lower appellate court disallowed the pre-emption was that the pre-emptor being a widow was not a co-sharer to claim any right of pre-emption u/s. 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as she has only a life interest in the property in question. Notwithstanding the fact that a widow has life interest in the property in question during her life time, she remains a full owner thereof with complete right of acquisition and dispensation subject to law. Such a widow can be safely said to be a co-sharer of any holding or of any property as contemplated u/s. 96(1) of the Stare Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In this connection reference may be made to section 3 of the Hindu Women’s Rights to the Property Act (XVIII of 1937). Sub-section (1) of section 3 of the said Act says that when a Hindu governed by the Dayabhag School of Hindu Law dies intestate leaving any property, his widow shall be entitled to same share as a son. Sub-section (3) of section 3 of the said Act further says that interest devolving on a Hindu widow shall be the limited interest but she shall have the same right of claiming partition as a main owner. 

 3. Considering the aforesaid provisions of sub-sections (1) and (3) of section 3 of the Hindu Women’s Rights to the Property Act (XVIII of 1937) it clearly appears that during the period of her life time a Hindu widow is a complete owner and co-sharer of any property or holding in question with the right to claim partition and consequently having the right to claim pre-emption u/s 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In this connection it may be mentioned that it has been represented that Mostafa Kamal, J. sitting singly in another Bench has held the same view in Civil Revision Case No. 98/1978 by his Judgment dated 4th February, 1982. 

 Be that as it may, for the foregoing reasons stated hereinbefore the decision of the Sub-ordinate Judge of Pabna made on 31st December, 1976 in Misc. Appeal Nos. 31 and 32 of 1975 must be held to suffer clear error of law on the face of the records and is accordingly set aside. The decision made by the its Munsiff of Serajganj by Order No. 67 dated 30.4.75 in Misc Case Nos. 94 and 95 of 1970 allowing pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is restored.
